subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which enzyme breaks down starch into sugars?
questions.explain: Amylase is a carbohydrase that digests starch into simple sugars such as maltose.

questions.q: Bile is stored in which organ before release into the small intestine?
questions.explain: Bile made in the liver is stored in the gall bladder until needed.

questions.q: What is the main role of the stomach in digestion?
options: Produces hydrochloric acid and protease to begin protein digestion
questions.explain: The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid and the protease pepsin to start digesting protein.

questions.q: Where is amylase first produced in the digestive system?
questions.explain: Salivary glands make amylase, which begins starch digestion in the mouth.

questions.q: Where does most chemical digestion of food finish?
questions.explain: Enzymes from the pancreas and small intestine complete digestion in the small intestine.

questions.q: How are villi adapted for absorption?
options: No blood supply to slow diffusion
Large surface area and thin walls with good blood supply
questions.explain: Villi give a large surface area, have thin walls and a rich blood supply for efficient absorption.

questions.q: Where is most digested food absorbed into the blood?
questions.explain: The small intestine is adapted with villi to absorb digested food molecules.

questions.q: What is the role of fibre in a balanced diet?
options: Helps food move through the gut and prevents constipation
questions.explain: Dietary fibre is not digested but keeps food moving through the intestines.

questions.q: Why does the stomach produce hydrochloric acid?
options: To provide the optimum pH for stomach protease and kill bacteria
questions.explain: The acidic conditions kill pathogens and give the right pH for the protease in the stomach to work.

questions.q: A balanced diet should contain water, fibre and which group of main nutrients?
options: Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins and minerals
questions.explain: A balanced diet supplies carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre.

questions.q: Which nutrient is mainly needed for growth and repair of tissues?
questions.explain: Proteins provide the amino acids needed to build and repair body tissues.

questions.q: Where is bile made?
questions.explain: Bile is produced in the liver and then stored in the gall bladder.

questions.q: Lipase digests lipids (fats) into which products?
questions.explain: Lipase breaks lipids down into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: Which organ produces amylase, protease and lipase?
questions.explain: The pancreas makes all three types of digestive enzyme and releases them into the small intestine.

questions.q: What does protease break protein down into?
questions.explain: Protease enzymes digest proteins into amino acids.

questions.q: Why does the large intestine play a role at the end of digestion?
options: It absorbs water from undigested food to form faeces
It absorbs amino acids into the blood
questions.explain: The large intestine absorbs water, leaving solid faeces to be egested.

questions.q: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the primary energy source in a balanced diet.

questions.q: Why does breaking large food molecules into smaller ones help the body?
options: Small soluble molecules can be absorbed across the gut wall into the blood
questions.explain: Digestion makes molecules small and soluble enough to be absorbed into the bloodstream.

questions.q: Which type of enzyme are amylase and other carbohydrases?
questions.explain: Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts.

questions.q: In the food test, what colour does Benedict's solution turn when heated with a reducing sugar?
questions.explain: Benedict's solution turns from blue to brick-red/orange when a reducing sugar is present.

questions.q: Which statement about bile is correct?
options: It is made in the pancreas
It is an enzyme that digests fat
It emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid
It breaks protein into amino acids
questions.explain: Bile is not an enzyme; it emulsifies fat and is alkaline so it neutralises acid from the stomach.

questions.q: Why does emulsifying fat by bile speed up its digestion?
options: It increases the surface area of fat for lipase to act on
Bile chemically digests the fat itself
It absorbs the fat into the blood
questions.explain: Bile breaks large fat droplets into smaller ones, giving lipase a larger surface area to work on.
